issue.title: Flaky test_headless_epic_approval_submits_while_inflight_launch_holds_anchor under the full parallel lane
issue.description:
tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py::test_headless_epic_approval_submits_while_inflight_launch_holds_anchor fails intermittently under the full parallel test lane and passes on a focused rerun. 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' at HEAD 6000a54a1 reports it as a reproducible flake exceeding tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

EVIDENCE (durable selection store ~/.sase/test-selection/gh_sase-org__sase/, read 2026-08-17 while landing epic sase-ns.6): 12 full-run failure records spanning 2026-08-06T13:35:09Z to 2026-08-17T01:37:59Z, recorded from six different workspaces (sase_10, sase_11, sase_12, sase_16, sase_17, sase_18) at twelve different HEADs with pairwise-disjoint changed-file sets, including runs whose only other failure was this node. That is the evidence shape the flake gate requires (two eligible full runs with disjoint change sets plus an interleaved independent pass), so this is reproducible flakiness rather than a single-run blip. Two of the twelve are from the last 24 hours (2026-08-17T01:24:38Z at HEAD 4819a0314 in sase_17, 2026-08-17T01:37:59Z at HEAD 4819a0314 in sase_20), so it is currently live.

SCOPE: reproduce under a contended full parallel lane (not a file-scoped 'just test-contention' run -- closed bead sase-mv records that file-level contention was green while the full lane was red), root-cause the shared state or timing dependency, and fix it without weakening the test's inflight-launch-holds-anchor assertion. The node name suggests a headless epic approval racing an in-flight launch that holds the workspace anchor, so the shared-state candidates are the approval lock/lease path and the agent-name or workspace claim registries.

The node has never been in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt; it is currently one of seven nodes keeping 'just check-full''s last gate red.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-ct — retired umbrella for ACE TUI full-parallel flakes; its close reason forbids +1 and directs narrow node-specific records like this one. This node is not ACE TUI, but the same routing policy applies.

RELATED: sase-j7 — in-progress epic owning process-global state leaking between tests. If the root cause here turns out to be a leaked global (approval lock, agent-name registry, or workspace claim), that epic's leak detector from phase sase-j7.2 is the right instrument. Filed as a narrow task rather than routed to sase-j7 because the node predates that epic (introduced 2026-08-02 by 186fd2010) and its failure mode has not been shown to be a global-state leak.

RELATED: sase-nd — sibling narrow full-lane flake task (test_run_supervisor_idle_timeout_fires_after_output_stalls). Both were surfaced together by the same selection-health gate run while landing epic sase-ns.6; not the same defect.

PROPOSED BY: phase sase-ns.6.1 of epic sase-ns.6 (Retire a fixed node's historical flake evidence), as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note on 2026-08-17T01:40:46Z. Routed to a new task bead by sase-ns.6's land agent.

Fixed by epic sase-ns.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.5 (commit b6246f1cf). Root cause: the test forked a multiprocessing 'fork' subprocess from a multi-threaded xdist worker to hold the epic plan launch lock -- a fork-after-threads hazard that could inherit a co-resident execnet receiver thread's state, which is why the node accumulated 12 pre-fix records across six workspaces at twelve HEADs. The fork is replaced by _foreign_epic_launch_lock_holder, an in-process context manager that takes fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on _epic_plan_launch_lock_path(anchor) and writes the same holder JSON the production epic_plan_launch_lock writes (pid/op/plan_file/started_at -- verified field-for-field against cli_work_from_plan_store.py:219-227). Because flock ownership belongs to the open file description rather than the process, the holder is indistinguishable from a foreign one; the helper self-checks this by asserting a second open() of the same path is refused with BlockingIOError before yielding. The inflight-launch-holds-anchor assertion is intact: the four patches are byte-identical (including resolve_beads_location's side_effect=AssertionError guarding against sidecar materialization), and start_launch.assert_called_once() plus the 'mon-contended' monitor-id assertion both survive. The one dropped assertion, process.exitcode == 0, tested the deleted harness subprocess rather than the code under test. Full-lane evidence: monitored just check-full swk45sjycf4e (31845 passed, 680.50s) did not name this node anywhere in its output. Land agent retired all 12 pre-fix records (newest 2026-08-17T01:37:59Z, all predating the fix) with a # fixed-at: 2026-08-17T08:54:01Z entry in commit cf7eeee03; just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake no longer names it.
